title: Supply Chain Resilience Mapping
business: Global logistics providers managing complex, multi-tier supplier networks.
problem: Traditional relational databases struggle to visualize deep-tier dependencies, leading to hidden bottlenecks when a single supplier fails.
solution: ArangoDB utilizes a multi-model approach, storing supplier entities as JSON documents and their interdependencies as edges in a graph, allowing AQL to traverse deep paths efficiently.
steps: Define supplier entities as document collections containing metadata like location and capacity.
Create edge collections to represent relationships such as 'supplies_to' or 'subcontracts_to'.
Populate the graph by inserting documents and linking them via edge documents containing _from and _to attributes.
Execute AQL queries using the GRAPH_TRAVERSAL function to identify all downstream dependencies of a specific supplier.
Analyze the resulting path objects to identify single points of failure in the supply chain.
outcome: Improved visibility into indirect supplier risks, enabling proactive diversification of the supply chain.
limitation: Graph traversal performance degrades significantly with excessive depth or high branching factors; verify this by monitoring the execution time of AQL queries using the PROFILE keyword.

It eliminates the need for JSON document storage.
It provides lower pricing for cloud hosting.
